cards.title: JWT and Tokens
cards.content:
JSON Web Tokens (JWT)

Authentication in single-page apps typically uses JWTs. Upon login, the server returns a token, which the client sends with subsequent requests.

Storage: Tokens can be stored in localStorage (vulnerable to XSS) or HTTP-only cookies (more secure against XSS, but requires CSRF protection).

cards.title: HttpInterceptors
cards.content:
HttpInterceptors

Angular's HttpInterceptor allows you to intercept outgoing HTTP requests and attach the JWT automatically to the Authorization header before the request leaves the app.

cards.title: Route Guards
cards.content:
Protecting Routes

Route Guards (like CanActivate) prevent unauthorized users from accessing certain routes. You can inject your Auth Service into a guard to check if the user is logged in or has the correct role.
